analysis: Changed behavior is confined to two small hunks in ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift, in the unload/retirement path. Head lines 1145-1149 restructure the Nemotron Super retirement branch so that on successful retirement `selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue(now: .now)` is called and the retired flag returned. Head lines 1213-1216 call the same method after a normal unload completes, following `retryReserveDeferredPrefetches()`. Both only schedule earlier retry checks for waiting selected models. They are scheduling hints and do not change admission, hashing, the weight-hash TOCTOU bracket, the add-on hold fences (`addonHoldLoadRefusal`), KV budget leases, SSD cache identity or any trust-boundary input. The call sits after the retire result is known, so the early-return behavior of the Super retirement path is preserved. The load path in the supplied base text (weight-hash capture, `finalizeReusableSSDLoad` fail-closed handling, pending-load lease, hold refusals before gate acquisition and before weight allocation) is unchanged. I reviewed it for context and found no regression against T-041, T-059, T-060, TB-007 or TB-012. Remaining unverified contract: `selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue` is defined outside the supplied evidence. I could not check that it is bounded, that it respects add-on hold state (T-059), or that it cannot trigger a load while a hold is active. The load path itself still checks `addonHoldLoadRefusal` before taking the load gate and again before weight allocation, so a recovery-triggered load should be refused during a hold. Making every selected model due after each unload could in theory cause a load/unload churn loop (availability, A-018), but there is no evidence of one in the supplied code, so I record it as a question for integration rather than a finding.
